summary.prose: Building this Story adds one family, ollama-claude, to the daemon's shipped model definitions and teaches the daemon to handle it: the catalog validator accepts a family marked as running a CLI on Ollama, the registry resolves a tier on it only to a declared model and refuses anything else with 'model-not-supported', and the definitions answer carries the new host and hosting marks. Every place that today means 'a vendor CLI family' is switched to 'has a CLI kind and no host', so the existing families behave exactly as before. The work ends by shipping the first six cloud models.

tasks.title: Catalog types and validator admit the Ollama-hosted family
tasks.summary: In src/daemon/model-catalog.ts: FamilyId gains 'ollama-claude' and FAMILY_IDS gains it; add HostFamilyId; FamilyDefinition gains host?: 'ollama' and ModelDefinition gains hosting?: 'cloud' | 'local'. Replace isCliFamily's 'id is not ollama' test with the family's shape: a host family must carry cliKind and host, must not carry tierDefaults or summariserModel, and every model needs hosting; a vendor CLI family keeps today's rules; hosting on any model of a family without host fails. The shipped definitions gain the ollama-claude entry here too (moved forward from t5), because the loader requires every family to be present. Grow the validator's test fixture to include ollama-claude (one cloud and one local model) alongside every existing family; later tasks reuse this fixture.

hosting on a vendor or plain-Ollama model fails validation.
The existing families validate exactly as before.

tasks.title: Registry exposes host and refuses undeclared host-family models
tasks.summary: In src/daemon/model-registry.ts: add host(family); FallbackReason gains 'model-not-supported' and TierResolution.model becomes optional. resolveTier on a host family resolves a declared model (id or alias, effort kept only if listed, otherwise reported as droppedEffort) and returns model undefined with fallback { reason: 'model-not-supported', requested } for an undeclared one, substituting nothing; the existing families keep today's path, with the unlisted/rejected fallback keyed on vendor families. familyForClient returns vendor families only. effortLevels over the five-family catalog keeps today's levels in today's order. Update the readers of resolution.model: resolveTierWith logs the refusal and tierModelOf reports the requested id (src/config/analyze.ts:232-247); the build-step validate fallback (src/daemon/steps/build-step/phases/validate.ts:195) keeps resolving the default vendor family.
